# Canned Tuna

Canned Tuna, canned from sauce-packed had total mercury higher at 380 µg/kg, against 153 µg/kg for water-packed in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rüstemli N, Tuncay R M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey">Mineral and heavy metal content in canned tuna: Implications for veterinary public health and consumer safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Veterinary Research Communications</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the canned Tuna came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

## What counts as canned Tuna

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers canned Tuna in 5 forms kept separate in every comparison: canned Tuna, canned (764 results), canned Tuna, oil (270 results), canned Tuna, as sold (63 results), canned Tuna, frozen (1 result) and canned Tuna, peeled or flesh (1 result).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-canned-tuna" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-canned-tuna-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of canned tuna, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach canned Tuna

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach canned Tuna comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Canned Tuna, canned from sauce-packed had total mercury higher at 380 µg/kg, against 153 µg/kg for water-packed in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rüstemli N, Tuncay R M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey">Mineral and heavy metal content in canned tuna: Implications for veterinary public health and consumer safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Veterinary Research Communications</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, canned Tuna, canned from packing-medium summary had total mercury higher at 227 µg/kg, against 188 µg/kg for all samples (summary mean) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shim2004-mercury-fatty-acids-canned-tuna-salmon-mackerel|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shim SM, Dorworth LE, Lasrado JA, Santerre CR · 2004</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shim2004-mercury-fatty-acids-canned-tuna-salmon-mackerel">Mercury and Fatty Acids in Canned Tuna, Salmon, and Mackerel</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shim2004-mercury-fatty-acids-canned-tuna-salmon-mackerel">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Targeted canned Tuna, as sold samples in EURO had cadmium higher at 2,760 µg/kg, against 9 µg/kg for EURO in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, targeted canned Tuna, as sold samples in WPRO had cadmium higher at 15 µg/kg, against 11.8 µg/kg for WPRO in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, lead across 35 groups of canned Tuna ranged from 3 µg/kg (purchased in Denmark) to 830 µg/kg (purchased in Russia); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ulusoy2023-canned-tuna-toxic-metals|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ulusoy S · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ulusoy2023-canned-tuna-toxic-metals">Determination of toxic metals in canned tuna sold in developed and developing countries: Health risk assessment associated with human consumption</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Marine Pollution Bulletin</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ulusoy2023-canned-tuna-toxic-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 17 groups of canned Tuna ranged from 150 µg/kg (product MI1) to 430 µg/kg (product P-1); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kosker2023-canned-fish-turkey|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kosker AR, Gundogdu S, Esatbeyoglu T, Ayas D, Ozogul F · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kosker2023-canned-fish-turkey">Metal levels of canned fish sold in Türkiye: health risk assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kosker2023-canned-fish-turkey">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-canned-tuna" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-canned-tuna" data-question="How do heavy metals get into canned Tuna?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into canned Tuna?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, canned Tuna from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than canned Tuna from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rüstemli N, Tuncay R M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey">Mineral and heavy metal content in canned tuna: Implications for veterinary public health and consumer safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Veterinary Research Communications</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Canned Tuna, canned from sauce-packed had lead higher at 94 µg/kg, against 53 µg/kg for water-packed in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rüstemli N, Tuncay R M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey">Mineral and heavy metal content in canned tuna: Implications for veterinary public health and consumer safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Veterinary Research Communications</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rustemli2026-canned-tuna-mineral-heavy-metal-turkey">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-canned-tuna" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-canned-tuna" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in canned Tuna?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in canned Tuna?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, canned Tuna, as sold had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in EURO (9 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (11.8 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For total mercury, the lowest regional median was in WPRO (45 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (170 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-canned-tuna-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-canned-tuna-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in canned Tuna is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in canned Tuna is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 3 results from 2 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study|23]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">25th Australian Total Diet Study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Australia New Zealand</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported inorganic arsenic in canned Tuna, as sold from 18 results in 1 reporting region, with subgroup medians below 10 µg/kg, mostly non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
